releaseNotes:
10.3.0: built on Jakar.Extensions 10.12.0, which moved UserRights into the new Jakar.Users package; Jakar.SqlBuilder now depends on Jakar.Users (10.1.0) for CommandParameters.Add(string, UserRights?). Source compatible (the type keeps the Jakar.Extensions namespace), but assemblies compiled against 10.2.0 must be rebuilt.
10.2.0: built SQL is laid out for people to read by default (SqlBuilderOptions.Layout = SqlLayout.Readable): each clause starts a line, a list with more than one item puts each item on its own indented line, AND / OR in conditions start indented lines, and CREATE TABLE / INSERT column lists, a single VALUES row and subqueries open indented blocks. Only the whitespace between tokens changes (literals, quoted identifiers, comments and dollar-quoted bodies are copied as they are) and the layout allocates nothing beyond the result. Use SqlBuilderOptions.Compact (Layout = SqlLayout.Compact) for the previous one-line form; code that compares built SQL text with one-line strings needs Compact or new expectations. New: SqlFormatter.Format(sql, dialect) applies the layout to any SQL; SqlBuilderOptions.Readable and SqlBuilderOptions.Compact presets. In / NotIn take any ISpanFormattable (In<T>): numbers, Guids and dates are written inline in the dialect's literal syntax, and a type with no SQL literal (TimeSpan, enums, record ids, NaN) is bound; In / NotIn(string) and (char) bind every value as a parameter, and In('a') no longer writes the character's code (97) through the long overload. SqlBuilderOptions.StrictTypes is now on by default: typed comparisons (Where<T>, On<T>, Set<T>, ...) throw SqlBuildException (TypeMismatch) for a value of the wrong type, including every value of an IN list, and for IS NULL on a non-nullable column; set StrictTypes = false for the previous behavior. New: ISqlParameterValue<TValue> marks a wrapper that binds as TValue, so a column of that type compares as TValue (RecordID<T> is ISqlParameterValue<Guid>, AutoRecordID<T> is ISqlParameterValue<long>). Stages are single-use and share one pooled per-thread writer: continuing a stage that a later stage moved past, or one whose statement was already built or streamed, throws InvalidOperationException. Build() / BuildSql() can be called again on the same stage and return the same SqlResult; WriteTo on an unbuilt stage is final. Fixed: WHERE kept its clause flag when the comparison copied the writer.
